To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
parents of HIV-inflicted children reported lower QoL scores for their children than did parents of children who were uninfected.
HIV infection was associated in general with worse mean QoL, but uninfected children had worse psychological functioning.

HIV-infected children had worse health perceptions than did uninfected children; HIV-infected children and adolescents had worse functional and social/role domains; and no consistent QoI differences were observed among different treatment regimens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
quality of life of children infected with HIV.
the impact of HIV infection and treatment on the quality of life of children and adolescents.
the quality of life for children and adolescents who are infected with HIV and the impact of antiretrovial treatment on their quality of life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QoL is generally worse for HIV-infected children than for uninfected controls.
QoL is not a major problem for HIV-infected children and adolescents.
HIV-infected children and adolescents generally have worse QoL scores, compared with their uninfected counterparts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-infected children and adolescents are not uniformly impaired in their QoL.
the QoL of HIV-infected youth is generally similar to that of uninfected youth, although HIV-infected children and adolescents not receiving antiviral treatment have worse QoL.

the quality of life for HIV infected children and adolescent is generally lower than their uninfected peers and that the quality of the antiretrovirals used in treatment does not seem to affect this outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV-infected children have worse QoL than do uninfected children; however, HIV-infected children receiving antiretrovirals have QoL similar to that of uninfected peers.
the QoL of children living with HIV has improved over time, with many of the children now living into adolescence and adulthood.
HIV-infected children have lower scores on some QoL domains than do HIV-uninfected children.
